title: Graph Connectivity With Threshold
statement:
There are `n` cities numbered `1` to `n`. Two different cities `x` and `y` are joined by a two-way road exactly when some integer `z` with `z > threshold` divides both `x` and `y`. Each `queries[i] = [a, b]` asks whether city `a` can reach city `b` by following one or more roads.

Return a boolean array `answer` with one entry per query, in the same order: `answer[i]` is `true` if a path exists between the two cities of `queries[i]`, and `false` otherwise. The same pair may be asked more than once, and `[a, b]` means the same as `[b, a]`.
signature: List<Boolean> areConnected(int n, int threshold, int[][] queries)
notes:
## Intuition

A road exists between `x` and `y` when they share a divisor `z > threshold`. Turned around: for every allowed `z`, all multiples of `z` (`z`, `2z`, `3z`, ...) are pairwise joined. To know who can reach whom we only need connected components, not the roads themselves, so it is enough to join each multiple of `z` to `z`: that already puts the whole group in one component. A union-find structure keeps the components, and every query becomes "do the two cities have the same root?". Checking every pair of cities with a gcd and searching the graph per query also works, but costs O(n²) per query.

## Approach

1. `parent[city] = city` for every city: each starts alone.
2. `find(city)` climbs to the root, halving the path as it goes so later calls are fast.
3. For every `z` from `threshold + 1` to `n`, walk `multiple = 2z, 3z, ...` up to `n` and merge the roots of `z` and `multiple` when they differ.
4. For each query `[a, b]`, answer `find(a) === find(b)`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 6`, `threshold = 2`. For `z = 3` the only multiple is `6`, so `3` and `6` merge. For `z = 4, 5, 6` the first multiple `2z` is already beyond `6`, so nothing else merges. Query `[1, 4]`: different roots, `false`. `[2, 5]`: `false`. `[3, 6]`: same root, `true`. The answer is `[false, false, true]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n · α(n) + q · α(n)) roughly: the multiples of all `z` add up to n/1 + n/2 + ... ≈ n ln n merges, and each query costs two `find` calls.
- Space: O(n) for `parent`.

## Pitfalls

- `z` must be strictly greater than `threshold`: start at `threshold + 1`. With `threshold = 0`, `z = 1` divides everything and joins all cities.
- Do not build every pair of multiples as an edge; linking each multiple to `z` gives the same components with far less work.
- Start the inner loop at `2z`: `z` itself needs no link, and a `z` above `n / 2` has no multiple in range, so it changes nothing.
- A shared gcd is not required between the queried cities themselves; they may be connected through other cities (`15` reaches `28` via `3`, `12` and `4` when `threshold = 2`).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `parent` | union-find links; a root points to itself |
| `find` | returns the root of a city's component |
| `z` | a common divisor larger than `threshold` |
| `multiple` | a city that `z` divides, other than `z` |
| `rootZ`, `rootMultiple` | the two roots being merged |
| `a`, `b` | the cities of one query |

narration.2: Every city starts as its own component: its parent is itself.
narration.3: find returns the root of the component that holds city.
narration.4: Keep climbing until we reach a city that is its own parent.
narration.5: Path halving: point the city at its grandparent so later searches are shorter.
narration.10: Only divisors strictly greater than threshold create roads.
narration.11: Every multiple of z shares the divisor z with z, so it belongs to z's component.
narration.14: Merge only when the two cities are still in different components.
narration.15: Hang the multiple's component under z's root.
narration.19: Two cities are connected exactly when their components have the same root.
